title: A HARPS wave near 13.505 days reduces independent HIRES error by 17 percent for HD 1461
abstract: We test whether a known HD 1461 velocity signal transfers between instruments. A circular wave fitted to 245 HARPS nights reduces weighted error by 17.42 percent in 215 independent HIRES nights. A conditional 95 percent interval from 30-day blocks is 7.91 to 27.17 percent. The known 5.77-day signal gives a 32.52 percent gain as a positive control. A second HARPS reduction, a cubic trend, small period changes, and a linear HIRES activity term retain the gain. Period, phase, and amplitude come from HARPS only. HIRES baseline terms are fitted in both models. This supports transfer of the known signal. It does not find a new planet or exclude stable stellar activity. The intervals do not include training-wave uncertainty. We include original code, aggregate results, figures, exact input hashes, source attribution, and external retrieval steps. Source records and derivative record databases are excluded.
